cohort: The cohort consisted of 1022 late preterm infants (34 + 0 to 36 + 6 weeks gestational age) born between 2019 and 2021 at a single center, excluding infants with congenital anomalies expecting NICU admission.
finding: Escalation of care for late preterm infants most frequently occurs within the first 24 hours after birth, primarily due to the need for respiratory support, cardiorespiratory monitoring, and thermoregulation.
followup_time: During birth hospitalization (up to 133 hours post-birth for escalation events)
